findingDetails.title: Authored metadata can make generated routing escape its declared containment boundary
findingDetails.scopeProof: Prior correctness and security passes traced both escaping consumers and negative-test gaps; this traceability pass confirmed doctrine promises resolution, not containment.

claimAdjudication.claim: Authored standalone packet and choreography resource paths can resolve outside their documented roots while verified write paths remain confined.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Reused the completed security adjudication and checked whether doctrine falsely claims containment.
claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: Current authored values are contained, but that does not enforce the contract for future values.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: An always-executed upstream normalized/realpath containment boundary covers both consumers.

findingDetails.title: The authoritative CI fleet gate is not triggered by command-metadata-only changes
findingDetails.evidence: Both path-filter lists omit root command-metadata.json while the job runs the fleet gate at lines 101-110.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Compared both workflow filters with all seven root files and checked the separate local-hook coverage.

claimAdjudication.claim: A command-metadata-only push or pull request does not trigger the workflow that declares and runs the authoritative fleet metadata gate.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Reviewed both push and pull-request path filters for broader patterns, then checked the exact local pre-push gate and its bypass semantics.
claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: Another changed file can incidentally trigger the workflow, and ordinary local pushes run the pre-push gate; neither makes validation mandatory for a command-metadata-only pull request or bypassed push.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Another mandatory CI workflow invokes the same fleet gate for every command-metadata-only change, or both path filters are expanded.
